Block B9: Tire pressure problem. Given: initial pressure 5 atm, initial temperature 27°C, final temperature 54°C, volume constant. Need final pressure. So record with givens: P1=5 atm, T1=27°C, T2=54°C, V constant. Relationship: P/T = constant (ideal gas law for constant V). Conditions: ideal gas, constant volume.

Block B10: Same as B11 duplicate. It's a sealed container volume 12 L, nitrogen pressure 80 atm, temperature 17°C, molar mass 28 g/mol, ideal gas. Need mass of nitrogen. So givens: V=12 L, P=80 atm, T=17°C, M=28 g/mol. Relationship: PV = nRT, n = m/M, so m = (PV M)/(R T). Conditions: ideal gas.

Block B12: Syringe problem. Given: container volume 0.9 ml, contains 0.5 ml liquid, so gas volume initially? The gas volume initially = 0.9 - 0.5 = 0.4 ml. Pressure of gas in container initially = 10^5 Pa. Syringe: cross-sectional area 0.3 cm^2, length 0.4 cm, so volume of gas in syringe = area*length = 0.3 cm^2 * 0.4 cm = 0.12 cm^3 = 0.12 ml (since 1 cm^3 = 1 ml). Pressure of gas in syringe = 10^5 Pa. Temperature same, no change. After injecting, total gas volume = initial gas volume + syringe volume = 0.4 ml + 0.12 ml = 0.52 ml. Total moles constant, pressure changes. Use P1 V1 = P2 V2 (constant T). So final pressure = (P_initial * V_initial) / V_final = (10^5 Pa * 0.4 ml) / 0.52 ml = approx 7.69e4 Pa. So record with givens: container total volume 0.9 ml, liquid volume 0.5 ml, initial gas pressure 10^5 Pa, syringe cross-section 0.3 cm^2, length 0.4 cm, syringe gas pressure 10^5 Pa, temperature equal constant. Conditions: isothermal, ideal gas, volume additive. Relationship: P1 V1 = P2 V2.
